prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation. Supervisory, bay execution, protection layers separate; none substitutes another. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): sequencing, interlocks, timestamps; executes only approved-logic/interlock-permitted commands; validates mode/authority/availability; stale points degraded; receives Breaker Inspection Tag (Cinder), Battery Load Test Record (Station DC System); sends Bay Status Digest to Glasswing. North/South Bay Controllers: own bay; North blocks close without interlocks, local control without comms; South reports mode/availability. Breaker Control Unit: executes accepted commands, rejects unpermissive ones, returns position/health. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): protection independent of comms; sends Relay Diagnostic Note to Larkspur; testing keeps energized-feeder coverage. North Protection Panel: network-independent trips. Transformer Protection Panel: transformer-only. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): indications/command results with quality, no protection; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; receives Protocol Retry Summary. Station Gateway: external boundary; rejects/logs bad requests; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): synchronized/degraded/unavailable; sends Clock Drift Snapshot to Orchard; time-quality issues investigated before sequence analysis. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative time-ordered evidence, flags uncertain times. Maintenance Remote Terminal: authorized, no bypass; receives Settings Review Receipt. Station DC System: confirmed available before control-power switching. Engineering Workstation: authorized config under change control; produces Settings Review Receipt. Actors: Control Room Operator: decides automation appropriateness; produces Clearance Handoff Memo (to Keystone); tracks out-of-service protection; confirms locally when remote status incomplete/delayed. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): Isolation Boundary Card; checks memo vs switching record; confirms authority/state/comm limits before automation actions; handback. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): settings, post-change review, assesses unexplained trips before return. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): uses Isolation Boundary Card to verify boundary; works after clearance/isolation/grounding; reports anomalies, pauses if boundary uncertain. Substation Supervisor: authorization, change control; confirms records complete, restrictions cleared, risks owned before normal service. Requirements: local before remote; suspected faults assessed before restart/bypass/replacement; restoration confirms indications, protection, comms, test connections removed.

New part:
S240: The Maintenance Remote Terminal shall use controlled access, and each maintenance session shall be attributable to an authorized user.
S241: The North Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
S242: The South Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
S243: The North Protection Panel shall remain available for independent protection functions during supervisory control interruptions.
S244: The Transformer Protection Panel shall remain within its approved settings and operating constraints during handover.
S245: Periodic operational reviews shall examine command outcomes, event records, exceptions, and corrective actions so that automation decisions remain traceable and safe.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
